name: Adaptive regulation

subjectOf.text: Where jurisdictions are not compelled to agree on the same rule, some jurisdiction will try a different rule, and will do so more quickly, when changed economic circumstances make a different rule optimal.
subjectOf.abstract: diction will try a different rule, and will do so more quickly, than if all jurisdictions felt compelled to agree upon the same rule.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Reflections on the Possible Application of Contingent Capital in Corporate Governance (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=1998455
scope_conditions: where jurisdictions are not compelled to converge on a single rule
where underlying economic circumstances change so that a different rule would be optimal

subjectOf.text: Dynamic elements built into the regulatory structure would allow regulators to continually adapt to new market environments, to financial innovation, and to changes in financial markets that are themselves caused by financial regulation.
subjectOf.abstract: Dynamic elements in the regulatory structure may allow regulators to continually adapt to new market environments, financial innovation, and to changes in financial markets as a result of financial regulation.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857
scope_conditions: dynamic elements are incorporated into the regulatory structure

subjectOf.text: Contrary to criticism that blockchains are designed to dodge regulation, the authors argue the actual goal of decentralized supply chain recording is effective, efficient, adaptive regulation that ultimately exceeds the current level of oversight.
subjectOf.abstract: Contrary to the criticisms that have been lobbed against blockchains as being designed to dodge regulation, the actual goal is to ensure effective, efficient, adaptive regulation in a truly decentralized manner, ul- timately exceeding the current level of oversight.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Future of Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782201

subjectOf.text: Conventional governance methods that are reactive or fixed to ex-post solutions are insufficient for governing technologies whose behavior changes continuously after deployment.
subjectOf.abstract: These conventional methods, largely reactive or fixed to ex-post solutions, are proving insufficient for the dynamic nature of AI technologies.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Governance (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4796714
scope_conditions: holds for AI systems that continue to learn after release

subjectOf.text: Legacy ex-ante regulatory attempts fail because they assume a static technological landscape, while AI development is dynamic and requires rules that are adaptable and responsive.
subjectOf.abstract: The exponential pace at which AI technology evolves makes it difficult to establish legacy system ex-post regulations that remain relevant over time. In turn, legacy ex-ante regulatory attempts assume a static technological landscape.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Governance (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4796714
scope_conditions: applies to legacy ex-ante and ex-post rulemaking
holds under exponential rates of technical change
